note: Pins are the SHAs the reference corpus was last validated against. Advance only via tools/sync-external.mjs --advance.

vta-agent-memory-agent-connect.why: Keyring's own fork of vta-agent-memory, where the agent connect plugin work (plan D45, §7.6, track B) lands on branch integration/agent-connect before any of it goes upstream: pairing with the link and QR code and the owner's grant at the pinned VTA (PR-3b, 4057a5a). Reviews of Keyring's agent connect work read the plugin side here. A separate clone: the upstream entry vta-agent-memory stays at OpenVTC main 80047d9, the base the fork extends. `branch` names the branch sync-external digests and advances on, since the fork's default branch is main.

vta-browser-plugin.why: TSP 1.0: @openvtc/vti-tsp-js 0.4.0 (#374, a24e498) packs YTSP-BAA and refuses Rev 2 and Rev 3; its spec-v1-vectors.json is the 1.0 Appendix A the bridge build's codec is checked against (docs/plans/tsp-1.0-cutover-plan.md). The app's TSP oracle stays the vendored 0.3.0 build until the Rev 3 reader is removed.

verifiable-trust-infrastructure.why: Tag vta-service-v0.84.0 (vta-sdk 0.91.0), what every Farm VTA runs (0.84.0 per the nightly watch, 2026-11-24), matched as the plan owner's rule asks; 0.84.0 to 0.87.0 serves the same task set. On Alberto's word (2026-11-26). card-verify moved to this vta-sdk and to its Cargo.lock versions in the same pull request.

verifiable-trust-infrastructure-v047.why: A second, separate clone of VTI at tag vta-service-v0.47.0 (DTG Credentials v1, #1859): card-verify-v047 is built from it so bifold's vti-conformance job can have vta-sdk 0.58 judge the vetted/1 statement Keyring writes behind its off-by-default flag (228). The main pin above, its clone and the frozen lab do not move with it.

verifiable-trust-infrastructure-hcp.why: A third, separate clone of VTI at main 0cc18df23 (#2823, the merge that added docs/05-design-notes/hcp.md, blob 06537e4f6f8579a993996d6def00440b3fb10fe0), only to read the HCP V0 contract the agent connect work builds to (hcp.md §5.1, the consent-request effect kinds). No tagged release contains hcp.md yet: VTI-Fig (bf35b6787) was cut before it. The main pin above stays at what the Farm runs (Alberto's rule) and does not move with this one; nothing builds from this clone. This entry is removed once the main pin is a tagged release that contains hcp.md and the Farm runs it.

affinidi-tdk-rs.why: #967: affinidi-tsp 0.3.0, TSP 1.0 (YTSP-BAA), the Rust side the bridge build interoperates with. Since #949 (eafbd150) the mediator lives in its own repository, so this pin no longer holds the mediator's source; the lab builds its mediator from its own checkout (local-vti-stack, TDK_SRC) and does not move with this pin.

affinidi-messaging-mediator.why: The mediator's own repository since affinidi-tdk-rs #949. Pinned at v0.53.0's commit, the version the wallet mailbox runs (deploy/keyring-messaging/mailbox/Dockerfile pins the same commit in full), so what is read here is what was deployed and measured: the account and ACL rules, the config schema, the wake protocol. v0.53.0 is a tag on a release branch, not on main; upstream-watching reads main through sync-external.mjs, not this pin.

openvtc.why: Tag VTI-Eucalyptus: openvtc 0.5.0 (#481; no v0.5.0 git tag), vta-sdk 0.63.3, messaging-sdk 0.33.2. Carries the VTI-67 may_claim fix (#456) that v0.4.0 lacked.

dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf.why: AclEntry 0.3 (purposes), acl/list/0.4 and acl/{grant,revoke,update}/0.3: what VTI main 887370a3b serves and bifold #1005 sends; the previous pin predated them, so #1005's payload checks had to read unpinned origin/main

dtgwg-cred-spec.why: Upstream main at #94, Working Draft 0.7.0: the VDC (#19), the VAC (#29), the VSC with witnessed/1 (5a660ea), issuerScope (#30, #68, #74), the decided registry context IRIs (#64), Data Integrity securing and taskContext binding (#56), and the salt for context v3 (#87, v3 not yet published, so no salt is emitted). The previous pin predated all of these, though Keyring's VRC, VMC, vetting and witness code and agent connect's VDC (step 7.3) were already written against them.

predicate-credential-system.why: The source of the published crate predicate-credential-system 0.1.0 (tag predicate-credential-system-v0.1.0), so citations in the zero-knowledge work name a pinned commit. Main is 3 commits ahead with a dependency bump only (affinidi-did-resolver-cache-sdk 0.8.40), not yet released.

hcp-spec.why: Human Context Protocol 2.0-draft-3 (spec/2.0-draft-3/specification.md, schemas/2.0-draft-3/): the text the agent connect plan's HCP companion cites by section and line, and the commit the hcp/* Trust Task suite (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf #1380) carries. Not an OpenVTC repository, so it names its own URL.

vta-agent-memory.why: The agent connect plan's plugin (decision D45): Keyring's pairing, mediator session and chat, channel and inbox, sender gate and the hcp agent CLI are built by extending this repository, not a new one (plan §3.12, §7.6, §7.27 track B). Pinned at main, vta-sdk 0.94 and vti-secrets 0.43 (#63).

@openvtc/vti-tsp-js.tripwire: our noble HPKE is the shipped wire layer; any bump = crypto or CESR change — audit before adopting

@openvtc/pnm-core.tripwire: channel chain + consent surface; minor bump = wallet-facing API moved

@openvtc/trust-tasks.tripwire: the Cypress lock; any bump past 0.9.x = post-Cypress framework movement
